provenance.baseCommit: af18618 plus the finish-review fix batch
provenance.world: New replacement world (strip-chart recorder). Not seeded from a catalog world; no world/seededFrom carried. Supersedes the retired Ink & Signal look, which is not documented.
provenance.finishReview: ship: one fix round (8 material fixes) plus one regression (project ink contrast), all scored resolved by the finish reviewer before commit

headline.purpose: Fold titles on the landing; docs section headings at 700 2.15rem.

view-title.purpose: Dashboard and portal hero line with tabular digits.

figure.purpose: KPI values and single large figures (up to 40-44px).

title.purpose: Item headings in ledgers, steps, specs and tier cards.

body.purpose: Site reading copy; 1.65 line-height in docs.

mono.purpose: Code, commands, timestamps, paths, file names, durations, axis figures only.

narrative.overview:
Narrately is drawn as an instrument, not a dashboard. Every surface is a sheet of white chart paper printed with a cool green grid, written on by recorder pens at full strength, and held in a dark enamel chassis that carries the controls as engraved plates. The landing page is one roll of that paper fed by the visitor's scroll; the docs are the same paper with a printed margin; the local dashboard and the team portal are the instrument's readout, with the chassis as their sidebar or app bar.

Density follows mode. The landing (Persuade) and docs (Read) run large, ruled and spacious, with folds of 120px and a 17px reading body. The dashboard and portal (Operate) tighten to 15px body, 34-36px controls and ruled instrument strips of figures. Hierarchy comes from scale, rules and the grid, never from card chrome or tinted surfaces. Depth exists only where one sheet physically overlaps another.

Rejected outright, and confirmed in the build: shadows, blur, colour gradients (hard-stop gradients only print the grid), glow, pastel washes, and the dark dev-tool hero with a glowing screenshot over a bento grid. The previous identity ("Ink & Signal": near-black, acid lime, serif italic accents) is retired and nothing from it carries over.
keyCharacteristics: White chart paper with a green grid (major line every fifth) as the ground; recorder pens as the only saturated colour.
A dark enamel chassis band carrying navigation as engraved, bordered plates.
Condensed DIN-like display numerals and headings, plain humanist body, mono only for machine text.
Selected is a solid pen line; alternatives are dashed.
Focus is a double keyline: ink outline, paper gap, red ring.
Depth only by an offset sheet behind a sheet.
Light and dark sets, one shared preference key.

rules.name: The One Meaning Per Hue Rule
rules.body: On any one page a hue means one thing. In the portal, members own the pen colours (the seven-pen `PALETTE`) and projects are drawn in ink tones (`INKS`: ink, ink 2, ink 3, ink 4, with any remainder grouped as "Other" in ink 5), so a colour never names both a person and a project. Every data ink clears 3:1 against paper in both themes; grid, rule and print greens never draw data.

rules.name: The Full-Strength Ink Rule
rules.body: Pens are used at full strength as lines, dots, bars and text. They are never lightened into pastel fills or tinted backgrounds; the only washes are the 7-10% red and green softs behind diffs, drop targets and the setup banner.

rules.name: The Paper Prints Green Rule
rules.body: Anything the paper itself would carry pre-printed (scales, axis figures, date lines, group headings, label plates) is print green. Anything an event wrote is a pen.

rules.name: The Machine Text Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for what a machine emits: code, commands, timestamps, paths and figures in tables. Headings, labels and prose are never mono.

rules.name: The Fixed Digit Rule
rules.body: Body text runs with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every surface, so figures sit in fixed positions and a changed value reads as an event, not a reflow.

rules.name: The Overlapping Sheets Rule
rules.body: If something must look raised, put a second sheet behind it, offset 6px by 6px. Never a shadow, never a tonal lift.

rules.name: The Double Keyline Rule
rules.body: Focus is `outline: 1.5px solid ink; outline-offset: 2px` plus `box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px paper, 0 0 0 5.5px red`. Composite fields (input wrappers, chat bar, composer, docs filter) carry the same ring on `:focus-within` at 3px/4.5px and suppress it on the inner input.

rules.name: The Solid Choice Rule
rules.body: The committed choice is drawn solid; alternatives are dashed. Tabs and range selectors carry a 1.5px dashed underline in rule 2 and the active one a 2px solid red underline (a sliding glider in the dashboard range and portal tabs). Toggles, context chips and suggestion buttons are dashed until on or hovered, then solid.

dos: Do set every surface on paper with a green grid, and put navigation on the dark chassis as engraved plates.
Do use recorder red for the one primary action per view and for the selected state; hover primaries to ink.
Do draw the selected option solid (2px red underline or glider) and its alternatives dashed (1.5px rule 2).
Do use the double keyline for focus: 1.5px ink outline, 2px offset, 4px paper gap, 1.5px red ring.
Do raise a sheet only by putting an offset sheet behind it (6px, 6px, paper 2, same border).
Do keep monospace for code, commands, timestamps, paths and figures, and keep digits tabular.
Do give members pen colours and projects ink tones when both appear on one page.
Do support light and dark through `data-theme` and the shared `narrately.theme` key.
donts: Don't use shadows, blur, gradients as colour, or glow for depth or emphasis.
Don't lighten pens into pastel fills or tinted backgrounds.
Don't let one hue mean two things on the same page.
Don't set headings, labels or prose in monospace.
Don't round sheets or panels; corners stop at 2-3px on controls.
Don't bring back the retired near-black, acid lime and serif italic look.
